messages:
Alex (Support): raising from SUP-2982 — customer reports large p95/p99 regressions for their Dedicated pool (eu-west-1-dedicated-42). saw p95 go from ~420ms -> ~2.4s, p99 spikes 6–8s. started ~2026-12-03 09:12UTC. customer says requests time out in bursts and some fall back to hosted which they don't want. ticket: https://support.internal/issue/SUP-2982

Maya (SRE): thanks Alex. can you paste a sample request id or trace id? also need which model + typical seq len (prompt + expected tokens). any recent config changes to that pool?

Alex (Support): one trace id: req_86a3f2cdf. model: redwood/open-7b-v2-quant, typical input ~600 tokens -> gen 150. no config changes on customer's side. they did increase QPS earlier today.

Jordan (Runtime): looking at traces for req_86a3f2cdf — backend show long time in "attach/warmup" stage. timeline: enqueue -> provision request -> attach to instance (5.9s) -> model init/warmup (1.3s) -> start. attach latencies spiking. autoscaler logs show attach_latency P50=4200ms P95=7400ms across pool between 09:05-09:20.

Provisioner Bot: pool eu-west-1-dedicated-42 attach_log snippet: 
```
[09:07:21] attach_request id=att_0x12 status=pending
[09:07:26] cloud_attach returned ok elapsed_ms=5973 instance_id=i-0a12
[09:07:27] driver_init elapsed_ms=1323
[09:07:28] ready
```
mount failures none. attach retries: 0. cloud provider API rate limited region for 09:05-09:14 window.

Maya (SRE): so root cause looks like cloud attach delay + insufficient warm pool buffer. when attach waits 6s, p95 balloons. two parts to mitigation: immediate (soft) and changes to autoscale policy (medium term). immediate: 1) bump prewarm slot by +1 on the pool, 2) reduce attach backoff/cooldown so scale decisions are faster 3) temporarily route new requests to a spare dedicated pool for this customer or to hosted fallback deliberately (but need customer ok).

Lee (Oncall): can we avoid routing to hosted fallback — customer explicitly banned fallback for SLA — so we should avoid hitting fallback. alternative: move customer to reserved backup pool that already has warm GPUs. we have spare capacity in eu-west-1-dedicated-21.

Jordan (Runtime): I can execute quick mitigation. will run these commands (using rcli):
```
# add 1 prewarm slot, set min-available to 2
rcli pool update --pool eu-west-1-dedicated-42 --prewarm 1 --min-available 2
# lower attach backoff and cooldown to speed repeated attempts
rcli autoscale config set --pool eu-west-1-dedicated-42 --attach-backoff 1s --scale-cooldown 30s
# emergency route: soft-shift customer to backup pool
rcli route update --customer CUST-443 --target-pool eu-west-1-dedicated-21 --drain-delay 10s
```
I'll run now and post results.

Maya (SRE): note cost impact and possible transient churn while controller reapplies. monitor for attach storm. set alert for attach_fail_rate > 5% and prewarm_utilization > 90%.

Provisioner Bot: executed rcli commands. response: success. change-id=chg_7643.

Jordan (Runtime): watch live: attach P95 dropped from 7400ms -> 1100ms over next 8 minutes. pool prewarm now shows 1 reserved warm instance and min-available 2. routing update in progress; traffic shifting 10% -> backup pool. Grafana panels: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/xyz/attach-latency?orgId=1&var-pool=eu-west-1-dedicated-42

Alex (Support): customer on call; pinged them that we're doing this. they're ok with moving to backup pool for 30min while we investigate deeper.

Nina (Customer Success): what's the long term plan? customer will ask about guarantees and cost.

Maya (SRE): long term: tune autoscaler to maintain a small number of always-warm GPUs per customer pool based on QPS history, increase capacity headroom heuristic during region-level cloud API throttling, and add early-detection of cloud attach latency regressions (alert at region level). also need a safe fallback strategy that preserves customer preferences (i.e., no-hosted fallback if disallowed).

Jordan (Runtime): adding a background warmup job that preloads KV caches + a minimal model init for most-active pools — reduces warmup from 1.3s -> 0.3s in tests. also adjusting attach parallelism to 2 to avoid serial attach tail latencies. will open RFC.

Lee (Oncall): we should also add a quick guard: if attach latency > 4s and pending queue > 20, temporarily reject new routed requests with 429 and explanatory body to avoid head-of-line blocking. customer can retry after backoff. less bad than p99=8s.

Maya (SRE): agreed. Jordan, can you throw a short-lived 429 gating rollout? if yes, coordinate with support so we can explain to affected apps.

Jordan (Runtime): yes, rolling a feature flag now: `fast_attach_gate`. -> deployed to eu-west controllers in 30s. sample rejection body: `{ "error": "temporary congestion: try again" }`

Provisioner Bot: alert suppression window created for SUP-2982 to avoid noisy alerts during mitigation.

Alex (Support): after mitigation customer reports p95 back down to ~480ms and p99 < 1.2s after ~10 minutes. they saw a short blip during routing shift. closing interim incident and will track as follow-up to RFC.

Maya (SRE): closing notes / action items:
- Jordan: RFC for always-warm heuristics + attach parallelism and warmup job (ETA 1 week)
- Runtime: implement attach region-level health alert and per-pool prewarm budget tuning (ETA 3 days)
- SRE: add gating/reject pattern to runbook + dashboard (ETA 48h)
- Support/Nina: communicate postmortem and cost implications to customer, include optional dedicated prewarm subscription (ETA 48h)

Lee (Oncall): if we see cloud attach latency spike again, escalate to provider ops and open emergency CAPA.

Maya (SRE): thanks everyone. marking thread resolved for now. will add notes to SUP-2982 and link to postmortem once RFC done.

Alex (Support): thanks all :rocket:
